messages.claim: At current volume the move to embeddings is unjustified: the experience store contains 2 entries, the task corpus ~8 tasks, and the codebase's own spec gates a vector store on retrieval volume that does not exist yet.

evidence.observation: wc -l reports 2 lines -- the entire retrieval corpus is two experiences; any scorer, including exact string match, is adequate over N=2.

module docstring: 'No vector database (spec section 22). Lexical scoring over a local JSONL store is adequate at this volume... swap the scorer when retrieval volume actually justifies it, not before.'
_similarity is Jaccard over stopword-filtered term sets; the docstring's stated reason is auditability: 'unlike an embedding it can be explained to whoever asks why a given experience was shown.'

RetrievalResult.provenance records query_terms and per-item scores into the trajectory for audit; term-level provenance is only meaningful under a lexical scorer -- an embedding swap would need a replacement provenance story.
'Only introduce a vector database when semantic retrieval volume justifies it.'
8 task JSON files total; the population generating experiences is tiny.

unknowns: Whether Jaccard's known failure mode (zero score on synonymous-but-disjoint vocabulary, e.g. 'rate limiter' vs 'throttle') actually occurs in this task set -- no retrieval-quality measurement exists in the repo that I could find.
Expected growth rate of experience.jsonl per sprint, which determines when 'volume justifies it' triggers.
messages.recommended_action: Do not swap the scorer now. Instead measure the real risk: build a ~15-pair labeled relevance set from the existing task prompts (including deliberate synonym pairs), score with _similarity, and record how many relevant pairs fall below min_score=0.05. That number, not taste, decides if/when embeddings are needed. Note the contamination guards (same-task refusal, held-out exclusion) and MMR diversity are scorer-independent and survive either choice.

verification.metric: recall@3 of lexical Jaccard on a labeled relevant-pair set drawn from the actual task corpus
verification.expected_if_correct: lexical recall@3 >= ~0.8; synonym-miss cases rare or absent in this domain's vocabulary
verification.expected_if_wrong: lexical recall@3 materially below embeddings (e.g. <0.6) with multiple relevant pairs scoring 0.0 from vocabulary mismatch

messages.claim: Ran the real retriever over the real store and task corpus: the decision stays lexical, but the live defect is precision (harness-boilerplate false positives above min_score), the synonym zero-recall failure mode is confirmed reproducible, and an embedding swap would touch three coupled scales, not one function.

evidence.observation: Now 3 lines, not 2 (a run was added since the researcher counted) -- the store grows while we deliberate, but N=3 is still trivially below any volume gate.

evidence.source: experiment: ExperienceRetriever.retrieve() over all 6 tasks/*.json against the live store
evidence.observation: dev_rate_limiter retrieved fix_divide_bug_unguided/fix_divide_dev at scores 0.213/0.182/0.145 and dev_comms_visualizer at 0.090/0.077/0.061 -- all above min_score=0.05, so a rate-limiter task is shown calculator-bugfix experiences today. Overlapping terms are pure harness boilerplate: ['capability','encode','full','modify','passes','suite','test','tests'].

evidence.source: experiment: synonym probe ('The checks are broken. Repair the division routine in the arithmetic module')
evidence.observation: Retrieved nothing (score 0) against three stored calculator-divide experiences -- confirms the researcher's unknown #1: Jaccard's disjoint-vocabulary failure is real and reproducible. A partial-paraphrase probe still retrieved correctly at 0.375.

min_score (0.05), the PASS/FAIL multipliers (1.25/1.15/0.85), and the MMR redundancy term in _select_diverse all consume the same Jaccard scale; swapping to cosine-of-embeddings requires recalibrating all three, not just replacing _similarity (7 lines).

'Only introduce a vector database when semantic retrieval volume justifies it' -- the gate the researcher cited is confirmed in the spec, and line 99 lists a vector DB among things the basic system must NOT require.

unknowns: Whether IDF-weighted lexical scoring (which down-weights corpus-common boilerplate for free) would close the precision gap as well as embeddings would -- untested, and there is no labeled relevance data in the repo to test against.
Growth rate of experience.jsonl per sprint, so the volume gate has no measurable trigger yet.
messages.recommended_action: Keep lexical scoring. Two cheap fixes first: (1) extend STOPWORDS with harness boilerplate (test/tests/suite/passes/capability/modify/encode/full) or switch _similarity to IDF-weighted overlap, and (2) re-tune min_score upward -- the observed false positives are the defect users would actually notice, and embeddings are neither necessary nor sufficient for it. Researcher should propose a retrieval-quality measurement (labeled relevant/irrelevant task pairs) so 'volume justifies it' becomes a testable trigger instead of taste.

verification.metric: false-positive rate at min_score=0.05: count of retrieved experiences for tasks with no genuinely related prior run, before and after stopword/IDF fix
verification.expected_if_correct: dev_rate_limiter and dev_comms_visualizer retrieve zero calculator-bugfix experiences after the fix, while fix_divide_bug still retrieves fix_divide_dev at high score
verification.expected_if_wrong: boilerplate terms are not the driver: false positives persist after removing them, which would strengthen the case for semantic scoring

messages.claim: The verification I committed to in turn 1 now has a result: adding the eight observed boilerplate terms to STOPWORDS (runtime monkeypatch, no repo change) eliminates every cross-domain false positive while relevant retrieval survives -- the precision defect is vocabulary hygiene, not a lexical-vs-semantic gap, so it cannot be an argument for embeddings.

evidence.source: experiment: STOPWORDS |= {test,tests,suite,passes,capability,modify,encode,full}, rerun over all 6 tasks/*.json
evidence.observation: dev_rate_limiter, dev_comms_visualizer, dev_disagreement_flow, diagnose_latency_regression now retrieve [] (previously up to 0.213); fix_divide_bug still retrieves fix_divide_bug_unguided/fix_divide_dev at 0.125/0.122/0.085 and fix_divide_bug_unguided still retrieves fix_divide_dev at 0.625 -- exactly the expected_if_correct branch of my turn-1 verification block.

Relevant scores dropped (0.234 -> 0.125) because shared boilerplate inflated them too, but remain 2.5x above min_score=0.05 -- the fix does not cost recall on the one genuinely related pair in the corpus.

Baseline suite: 23 tests, all OK, including test_irrelevant_experience_is_not_retrieved and test_stopwords_are_ignored -- the contamination and refusal guarantees are covered by tests and are scorer-independent (same-task/held-out exclusion happens before scoring, retrieval.py:155-160).

unknowns: The synonym zero-recall failure remains under any lexical scorer (my turn-1 probe scored 0 and still does) -- only embeddings or query expansion would fix it, but there is no evidence yet that any real task pair in this workbench exhibits it.
Whether the hardcoded stopword extension generalizes, or whether IDF weighting (corpus-derived, no constants to maintain) is the right permanent form of the fix -- undecidable at N=3 experiences.
messages.recommended_action: Decision-ready from my side: stay lexical; land the boilerplate-stopword or IDF fix as a small PR with the false-positive regression test above. If the researcher wants the volume gate to be testable rather than taste, they should propose the measurement (labeled relevant/irrelevant task pairs plus a recall@k threshold that, once missed by lexical scoring on real data, triggers the embedding migration). Absent objection, my turn 3 will be the FINAL_REPORT recording this.

verification.metric: regression test: retrieval for a rate-limiter-style task against calculator-bugfix experiences must return empty; retrieval for a calculator-bugfix paraphrase must return the fix_divide experiences
verification.expected_if_correct: test passes with the stopword/IDF fix applied and fails on current main
verification.expected_if_wrong: false positives reappear as the store grows with new boilerplate vocabulary, which would argue for corpus-derived IDF over a hardcoded list
